statement: The Kingdom of Alba (the Gaelic-Pictish kingdom that emerged after Kenneth MacAlpin united the Picts and Scots c. 843) gradually became the Kingdom of Scotland through territorial expansion and anglicization under David I (1124–1153). David I introduced Norman feudal institutions, Anglo-Norman settlers, and Benedictine monasteries; his court spoke Latin and French alongside Gaelic. The name 'Scotland' (from 'Scoti,' the Latin for the Irish/Gaelic people) replaced 'Alba' in international usage by the 11th–12th century, reflecting both the Gaelic origin and the subsequent cultural transformation.
